summary.verdict: APPROVED — no blocking security issues found
owasp_coverage: A09 (Security Logging / PII) — PASS with 1 low note

anti_idor_redirect.detail: executionId for redirect originates exclusively from inFlightExecutionId(), which is scoped by (projectId, funnelId, subscriberId) — never from request input. The claimForRedirect CAS re-checks _id + subscriberId + funnelId + status-in(running,waiting,waiting_for_reply) + stepRunStatus=pending atomically. A mismatched subscriber or funnelId deterministically loses the CAS and returns null → no-op + LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST WARN. Anti-IDOR is enforced by TWO independent layers: the trusted probe and the atomic CAS predicate. Test coverage: redirect_mismatchedSubscriber_isNoOp (EngineIT) + redirect_casLost_isNoOp_andEmitsWarn (EngineIT).

fail_closed_projectId.detail: dispatchForSubscriber receives projectId from a trusted caller (pinned by ApiKeyAuthFilter in EventsController; execution.getProjectId() from the claimed doc in StepExecutor emitEvent path). matchingFunnels() calls funnelRepository.findByProjectIdAndTriggersTriggerTypeAndTriggersTriggerValueAndStatus(...) with projectId as the first filter — all matched funnels are guaranteed same-project. inFlightExecutionId() includes .and('projectId').is(projectId) in its criteria, so the returned executionId is scoped to the same project+funnel+subscriber triple. No cross-project execution can be redirected even if an attacker constructs a crafted event payload. enrollSpecificFunnel() performs an explicit projectId equality check on the resolved target funnel before any enroll action (line 408: !projectId.equals(target.getProjectId())).

log_injection_pii.detail: All new LOG_* constants (LOG_REDIRECT, LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST, LOG_REDIRECT_BROKEN_CURSOR, LOG_DISPATCH_REDIRECT, LOG_DISPATCH_NO_MATCHED_ELEMENT, LOG_DISPATCH_FUNNEL_ERROR) log only ids (executionId, funnelId, projectId) and exception class names — never event_name, triggerValue, matchKey, subscriber names, or any PII. Verified all log.warn/log.error/log.info call sites in both FunnelExecutionEngine and FunnelEventService for the new redirect path. matchedEntryStepId() warns with triggerType (a fixed taxonomy code, not the runtime event_name). FunnelTriggerServiceImpl logs only projectId and triggerType (not payload/triggerValue). No log injection surface from attacker-controlled string interpolation into log messages.

dos_loop_bound.detail: redirectExecution mutates an existing row — it does NOT create a new funnel_executions row and does NOT reset enrollDepth. The existing execution's enrollDepth is inherited unchanged, so the depth-cap backstop (originDepth > maxEnrollDepth) still applies to any auto-enroll chain spawned by redirect. A redirect-driven loop (EMIT_EVENT -> trigger -> redirect -> EMIT_EVENT ...) is bounded by the SAME drive() loop guards: (a) per-tick budget maxStepsPerTick trips FUNNEL_STEP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED → terminate(failed); (b) a MESSAGE step parks waiting_for_reply, requiring a human button press to continue. No new path around either guard was introduced. Fan-out ceiling (maxFanoutPerEvent) counts redirects and starts equally (handled++ in both branches). Test coverage: emitEventTriggerSelfLoop_terminatesAtBudgetOrMenuPark (EngineIT).

error_isolation.detail: redirectOrStart() wraps the entire per-funnel redirect/start decision in try/catch(Throwable) that logs LOG_DISPATCH_FUNNEL_ERROR (ids/codes only) and returns false — one funnel fault never aborts the fan-out loop or escapes dispatchForSubscriber. dispatchForSubscriber itself has an outer try/catch(Throwable) (LOG_DISPATCH_ERROR) so the webhook job and the /events API endpoint are never 5xx'd. The redirectExecution() method in the engine has no unchecked throws; broken-cursor terminal-fail is handled explicitly before drive() so it never propagates. CAS-loss is a no-op return, not an exception. EventsController has a belt-and-braces try/catch around the dispatch call. No new path introduces an unguarded throw.

findings.category: A09 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.title: LOG_DISPATCH_NO_MATCHED_ELEMENT logs triggerType — confirm it stays a category code and never includes matchKey
findings.code_snippet: log.warn("{} funnelId={} triggerType={}", LOG_DISPATCH_NO_MATCHED_ELEMENT, funnel.getId(), triggerType);
findings.description: The WARN log for a missed re-scan includes triggerType (e.g. 'event'). triggerType is a fixed 5-value taxonomy (on_start/event/keyword/tag_added/custom_field_set) chosen by the funnel author at design time, not a runtime user value — it classifies as a code per Decision 16, not PII or a business secret. However, if this log line is ever extended to also emit matchKey/triggerValue to aid debugging, it would leak the event_name (a business-defined slug) to logs, violating Decision 16 and potentially leaking internal event taxonomy to log aggregators.
findings.impact: No current PII or business-secret leakage. Risk is forward-looking only: a careless future edit could add matchKey to this log line.
findings.recommendation: No code change required. Add a comment at the log site explicitly noting that matchKey/triggerValue MUST NOT be added here (same guard comment pattern as the existing 'never the event_name/triggerValue' comment block at L89-94 of FunnelEventService). Current code is compliant.

findings.category: A01 — TOCTOU on redirect path (benign by design)
findings.title: Two-step probe+CAS for redirect is a documented TOCTOU — confirmed benign, defense-in-depth holds
findings.description: inFlightExecutionId() performs a findOne (read), then redirectExecution() performs a separate findAndModify (write). A row visible in the probe could be claimed by the sweep or otherwise mutated between the two operations. This is NOT a vulnerability: (1) the executionId is sourced from a project+funnel+subscriber-scoped trusted probe, not from request input; (2) the CAS re-verifies _id, subscriberId, funnelId, status-in(running,waiting,waiting_for_reply), and stepRunStatus=pending atomically — no state corruption is possible even if the probe's snapshot is stale; (3) worst case is a no-op redirect (logged as LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST), which is the explicitly designed outcome per Decision 4.
findings.impact: None. At most an occasional no-op redirect under concurrency, fully covered by the CAS + WARN log. This is the intended best-effort-no-op design.
findings.recommendation: No change required. Document this as a known-benign TOCTOU with defense-in-depth. The CAS is the authoritative security gate. Test redirect_casLost_isNoOp_andEmitsWarn confirms the no-op property under concurrency.

findings.category: A01 — inFlightExecutionId probe does not filter stepRunStatus
findings.title: inFlightExecutionId can return an in_progress (sweep-owned) execution id — confirmed safe by CAS design
findings.description: The inFlightExecutionId query filters status IN (running, waiting, waiting_for_reply) but does NOT filter on stepRunStatus. This means it can return the id of a row currently owned by the sweep (stepRunStatus=in_progress). The subsequent claimForRedirect CAS requires stepRunStatus=pending, so such a row will lose the CAS, logging LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST — a no-op. This is the correct and intended behavior per Decision 4 (CAS-loss is best-effort no-op). The probe not filtering stepRunStatus is consistent with the intent: 'does a row exist for this (project, funnel, subscriber) triple in an in-flight status?' — the CAS is the only place that actually gates on pending.
findings.impact: No security impact. The probe being wider than the CAS is the design: it identifies the candidate row; the CAS decides whether the redirect can proceed atomically. No state corruption possible.
findings.recommendation: No change required. This is a documented design choice. The CAS is the authority. The no-op + WARN path is tested in redirect_casLost_isNoOp_andEmitsWarn.

verified_properties.executionId_source: executionId passed to redirectExecution comes ONLY from inFlightExecutionId() trusted probe — verified no request-input path
verified_properties.cas_predicate_binding: claimForRedirect binds _id + subscriberId + funnelId + status IN (...) + stepRunStatus=pending — all 5 conditions verified in code at lines 407-412 of FunnelExecutionEngine.java
verified_properties.cross_project_enrollment: dispatchForSubscriber receives projectId from trusted caller; matchingFunnels pins projectId as first filter; inFlightExecutionId includes projectId; enrollSpecificFunnel does explicit projectId equality check — no cross-project execution path found
verified_properties.pii_in_logs: All 6 new LOG_* constants emit ids/codes only — verified all log call sites in FunnelEventService and FunnelExecutionEngine; no event_name/triggerValue/matchKey/subscriber field logged on any redirect path
verified_properties.dos_no_new_row: redirectExecution calls findAndModify (no insert); enrollDepth unchanged; fan-out ceiling counts redirects; drive() budget and menu-park gate unchanged — no new path around loop bounds
verified_properties.error_isolation: redirectOrStart() try/catch(Throwable) + dispatchForSubscriber outer try/catch(Throwable) — redirect fault cannot escape to webhook/API; verified no unchecked throws in redirectExecution
verified_properties.bean_cycle: @Lazy on FunnelExecutionEngine in FunnelEventService constructor — Spring deferred proxy breaks the FunnelEventService→FunnelExecutionEngine→StepExecutor→FunnelEventService cycle; context startup is safe
